about.title: about
about.paragraph_1: the exhibition is organised as three thematic container-blocks reflecting different aspects of contemporary, digitalised truck-driver subculture. the mood evolves from playfully ironic to profound and thought-provoking, creating an emotional trajectory for the viewer. the exhibition includes works in different media, from three-dimensional art objects to flat poster-based pieces, forming a layered visual narrative about the contemporary truck driver.
about.paragraph_2: the works present a metaphor for the “load” truck drivers carry in both the literal and figurative senses. this load consists of kilometres of road and tonnes of freight, the profession’s distinctive aesthetics, unwritten rules, hardship, loneliness, constant tension, and the impossibility of leaving the route. the load becomes a universal symbol: it cannot be discarded, it is always behind one’s back, and the person themself is the one who drags it along.
about.section_1:
section i: “attributes”
the introductory part reinterprets objects from truck-driver aesthetics. the container brings together works that interpret professional jargon, everyday rituals, and objects of identity. art objects coexist with readymades and authentic elements of truck-driver paraphernalia. the section introduces viewers to this world and establishes an ironic, positive tone.
about.section_2:
section ii: “women”
the central part contains works examining the place of women in this professional environment. it reveals a range of female images, from loving mothers and wives to idealised sexual symbols. the container retains elements of irony while guiding the viewer towards deeper reflection and leaving room for personal interpretation.
about.paragraph_3: the image of women in the truck-driving profession is dual: on one hand, images of women remind drivers of family warmth, peace, and domestic comfort, often absent on long journeys. on the other hand, this image is frequently associated with sexualised depictions of women, distorting its original meaning—to symbolise support, comfort, and emotional reassurance.
about.section_3:
section iii: “loneliness”
the final part radically changes the exhibition’s emotional tone. the container holds a single work embodying the profession’s darker side. loneliness, emptiness, isolation, and numbing boredom concentrate at the final point of the route, creating a powerful emotional resonance.
